subject: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification for EdgeFin trial
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@edgefin.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@edgefin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification for EdgeFin trial

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet the EdgeFin team. Quick recap and proposed next steps around the performance/SLO qualification so we all have the same expectations before the benchmark run.

Recap / goals:
- Target production SLOs: 95th pct latency <= 200ms for single-turn generation (streaming enabled), 99th pct <= 400ms for 1k-token sequences.
- Target throughput: sustained 800 generated tokens/sec across the pool at peak concurrency.
- Concurrency: expected 250 concurrent user sessions (avg request size ~120 tokens; streaming chunked at 20 tokens).
- Streaming requirement: clients rely on partial tokens for UI; must support chunked streaming with <50ms per-chunk latency once generation starts.
- Measurement window: we recommend 30-minute sustained runs and three repeat runs for reproducibility.

Open items we need you to confirm (asks):
1) Final prompt set for the trial (you mentioned ~300 prompts). Can you confirm or send the finalized JSON?
2) Data sensitivity: any PII in prompts/outputs? If so we'll use a scrubbed dataset and run in isolated Dedicated mode.
3) Preferred time window for the benchmark run (we're flexible but would like a 2-hour window).
4) Any additional success criteria beyond latency/throughput (e.g., quality/regression thresholds, token-level ROI).

Next steps (our side):
- We'll provide the benchmark harness (Docker + runbook) and a reproducible measurement definition (seeded prompt replay, fixed seq lengths, and noise map).
- Share the harness and prompt set via Drive + attachment. Looking to schedule a canary run 24–48h before the main run.

Attachments: edgefin-prompt-set-v2.json (placeholder), SLO worksheet (slo-requirements.xlsx).

If the above looks good, confirm items 1–3 and we’ll drop the harness for your infra team to validate.

—
Marissa Cole

From: Samir Rao <samir@edgefin.com>

Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification for EdgeFin trial

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers/clarifications from our side: 

1) Prompt set: attaching the latest sanitized prompt pack (see edgefin-prompt-set-v2.json). ~320 prompts after sanitization. No customer PII in this set.
2) Streaming: yes, streaming is required. Our frontend renders partial tokens; the <50ms chunk latency is ideal.
3) Concurrency: the 250 concurrent sessions is accurate; we expect burst patterns around 11:30–12:30 PT next Wednesday (preferred run).
4) Quality thresholds: we want no more than a 2% regression in generation accuracy on the evaluation prompts relative to our current baseline. We'll share baseline eval metrics before the run.

We also have a compliance ask: can the harness run on a Dedicated test node that’s isolated (no external egress) for the official run? If yes, we’ll provide access details.

Look forward to the harness and the runbook. Also would like the measurement definitions — specifically how you compute 95/99 pcts for streaming responses (per-chunk vs end-to-end).

—
Samir Rao
Director of Product, EdgeFin Solutions
samir@edgefin.com | +1 212-555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification for EdgeFin trial

Samir — thanks, all good notes. Per your asks, we’ve attached the harness and a detailed measurement README. Key items included in the package:

- redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.tar.gz (Dockerfile + run scripts + sample config)
- runbook: how we seed, replay, and capture metrics (attached in Drive and included as README)
- measurement definitions (included in README):
   * Latency measurement: we report both per-chunk latency (time from token generation to chunk emit) and end-to-end request latency (time from request start to final token).
   * For SLOs we use end-to-end latency for 95/99 pcts, and we publish per-chunk 50/95 as a diagnostic.
   * Token throughput: measured as generated tokens/second, aggregated across worker pool, reported as moving-average over 1s windows.
   * Reproducibility: harness seeds random samplers; we run 3 full passes with identical seeds and compare distributions (KS test) to flag nondeterministic variance >3%.

Run instructions (short):
1) untar harness, build Docker image: ./build.sh
2) configure edgefin-prompt-set-v2.json path in config.yaml
3) run: ./run_benchmark.sh --duration 1800 --concurrency 250 --streaming true --seed 42

We’ll also push the Drive folder (link below) with the same assets and an annotated example result CSV. For the Dedicated test node: we can run the harness inside your isolated node if you provide a temporary container registry access and a minimal network allowlist; otherwise we can run from our Dedicated tenant with network controls.

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/benchmarks/EDGE-058
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/records/EDGE-058

Please confirm the preferred run window (you mentioned Wed 11:30–13:30 PT). We’ll schedule a canary 24h prior (short 15m run at reduced concurrency) to validate configs.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.tar.gz (application/gzip)], edgefin-prompt-set-v2.json (attached), slo-requirements.xlsx (attached).
